[P2] Stop accepted executions even without worker evidence

An accepted asynchronous invocation can remain queued or fail its initial evidence write, leaving no event containing its marker. This cleanup set then omits it, and `load_markers()` filters the service's running-execution list using that same incomplete set. Consequently, `close_case()` never stops the execution; it can keep settlement from completing and block subsequent deployments of the persistent fixture. Include outstanding test executions discovered through the service or invocation records without requiring worker evidence first, and cover an accepted execution with an empty event prefix.
